description: The negative priming paradigm, originally designed by Tipper (1985), rests on the logic that \"if a distractor (or a strategy) is inhibited on a given item (i.e., the prime), then its activation on the following item (i.e., the probe) should be disrupted\".
title: Negative priming paradigm adapted to misleading strategies

description: This framework conceptualizes design judgment as the ability to gain subconscious insights abstracted from experience and reflection in complex, indeterminate situations, and identifies multiple forms of judgment exercised across design situations.
title: Nelson and Stolterman's typology of design judgment operationalized for instructional design practice

description: Network meta-analysis (NMA) is presented as \"a new type of meta-analysis, which can compare the effectiveness of multiple interventions more intuitively and in detail, while traditional meta-analysis can only compare them in pairs\".
title: Network meta-analysis

description: The article recommends encoding pedagogically motivated constraints as learnable-weight symbolic rules that modulate neural predictions when simple evidence patterns occur in the interaction history.
title: Neural-symbolic knowledge tracing with conservative mastery and non-mastery rules

description: Adapting Newell's bands taxonomy from cognitive science, the article proposes that SRL phenomena be matched to the time scale at which they are theorized to occur: cognitive-band events over seconds observed with trace methodologies and think-alouds, rational-band events over minutes to hours includ
title: Newell-inspired time-scale taxonomy for aligning SRL measurement to theorized process duration
